verses.text: “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?
lines: “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth?
Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?

verses.text: Can you count the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they give birth?
lines: Can you count the months that they fulfill?
Or do you know the time when they give birth?

verses.text: They bow themselves. They bear their young. They end their labor pains.
lines: They bow themselves. They bear their young.
They end their labor pains.

verses.text: Their young ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They go out, and don’t return again.
lines: Their young ones become strong.
They grow up in the open field.
They go out, and don’t return again.

verses.text: “Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,
lines: “Who has set the wild donkey free?
Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,

verses.text: whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?
lines: whose home I have made the wilderness,
and the salt land his dwelling place?

verses.text: He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.
lines: He scorns the tumult of the city,
neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.

verses.text: The range of the mountains is his pasture, He searches after every green thing.
lines: The range of the mountains is his pasture,
He searches after every green thing.

verses.text: “Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?
lines: “Will the wild ox be content to serve you?
Or will he stay by your feeding trough?

verses.text: Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?
lines: Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness?
Or will he till the valleys after you?

verses.text: Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him your labor?
lines: Will you trust him, because his strength is great?
Or will you leave to him your labor?

verses.text: Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed, and gather the grain of your threshing floor?
lines: Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed,
and gather the grain of your threshing floor?

verses.text: “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly; but are they the feathers and plumage of love?
lines: “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly;
but are they the feathers and plumage of love?

verses.text: For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms them in the dust,
lines: For she leaves her eggs on the earth,
warms them in the dust,

verses.text: and forgets that the foot may crush them, or that the wild animal may trample them.
lines: and forgets that the foot may crush them,
or that the wild animal may trample them.

verses.text: She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,
lines: She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers.
Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,

verses.text: because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.
lines: because God has deprived her of wisdom,
neither has he imparted to her understanding.

verses.text: When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.
lines: When she lifts up herself on high,
she scorns the horse and his rider.

verses.text: “Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?
lines: “Have you given the horse might?
Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?

verses.text: Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.
lines: Have you made him to leap as a locust?
The glory of his snorting is awesome.

verses.text: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.
lines: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength.
He goes out to meet the armed men.

verses.text: He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.
lines: He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed,
neither does he turn back from the sword.

verses.text: The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.
lines: The quiver rattles against him,
the flashing spear and the javelin.

verses.text: He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.
lines: He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage,
neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.

verses.text: As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
lines: As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’
He smells the battle afar off,
the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

verses.text: “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?
lines: “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars,
and stretches her wings toward the south?

verses.text: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?
lines: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up,
and makes his nest on high?

verses.text: On the cliff he dwells, and makes his home, on the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.
lines: On the cliff he dwells, and makes his home,
on the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.

verses.text: From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.
lines: From there he spies out the prey.
His eyes see it afar off.

verses.text: His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”
lines: His young ones also suck up blood.
Where the slain are, there he is.”
